item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00281","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C16","C12"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C13 is a concrete and material template for the child. Both proclamations identify a bilateral trade agreement made under section 350(a), identify the earlier proclamation carrying it out, recite an agreement with the foreign government affecting the agreement’s continued force, invoke section 350(a)’s authority to terminate the implementing proclamation, and then declare that proclamation ineffective after a specified date. The child substantially compresses and adapts this same legal and drafting sequence from Brazil to Colombia. C16 has somewhat analogous termination-of-suspension machinery, while C12 concerns the same trade-agreement statute and termination language, but neither matches the child as closely as C13.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas under the authority vested in him by section 350(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930 ... the President ... entered into a trade agreement with the President of the Republic of Colombia ... and proclaimed such trade agreement by proclamation dated April 20, 1936","parent_excerpt":"Whereas, pursuant to the authority conferred by section 350(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930 ... the President ... entered into a trade agreement with the President of the Republic of the United States of Brazil ... which trade agreement was proclaimed by the president on December 2, 1935","explanation":"Distinctive parallel recital identifying the same statutory authority, a bilateral presidential trade agreement, and the proclamation that implemented it."},{"child_excerpt":"Whereas the Government of the United States of America has agreed with the Government of the Republic of Colombia that the said trade agreement shall cease to be in force","parent_excerpt":"Whereas, the government of the United States of America has agreed with the Government of the United States of Brazil that said trade agreement ... shall be inoperative","explanation":"Both use an intergovernmental agreement about cessation or inoperativeness as the factual predicate."},{"child_excerpt":"Whereas the said section 350(a) ... authorizes the President to terminate in whole or in part any proclamation carrying out a trade agreement entered into under such section","parent_excerpt":"Whereas the final sentence of said section 350(a) ... authorizes the President to terminate in whole or in part the proclamation carrying out any trade agreement entered into under section 350(a)","explanation":"This is nearly identical, legally specific authorization language."},{"child_excerpt":"do hereby proclaim that the said proclamation dated April 20, 1936, shall terminate and cease to have effect at the close of November 30, 1949","parent_excerpt":"do hereby proclaim that said proclamation of December 2, 1935 shall not be in effect after July 30, 1948","explanation":"The operative clause uses the same mechanism:
